record.paper_title: An update on Weihrauch complexity, and some open questions
record.original_question: For the algebraic structure of the Weihrauch degrees with signature (W; 0, 1, ⊤; ⊓, ⊔, ×, ⋆, →, ∗, b, ⋄), what can be said about the first-order theory Th(W; 0, 1, ⊤; ⊓, ⊔, ×, ⋆, →, ∗, b, ⋄)? In particular, is the quantifier-free part of this theory finitely axiomatizable, and do any fragments of the signature admit finite axiomatizations?

evidence.quote: Open Question 2. What can we say about Th(W; 0, 1, ⊤;⊓,⊔, ×, ⋆,→, ∗ , b, ⋄ )? Is its quantifier-free part finitely axiomatisable? What about fragments of the signature?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{W}$ denote the partially ordered set of Weihrauch degrees, that is, equivalence classes of multivalued functions between represented spaces under Weihrauch reducibility $\le_{\mathrm{W}}$ (where $f \le_{\mathrm{W}} g$ iff there exist computable maps $H, K$ such that for every realizer $G$ of $g$, the map $x \mapsto H(x, G(K(x)))$ is a realizer of $f$). Consider the algebraic structure
$$(\mathcal{W};\, 0,\, 1,\, \top;\, \sqcap,\, \sqcup,\, \times,\, \star,\, \to,\, {}^{*},\, \mathrm{b},\, \diamond),$$
where $0$ is the degree of the nowhere-defined problem, $1$ is the identity, $\top$ is the top degree; $\sqcap$ and $\sqcup$ are the infimum (parallel product with choice) and supremum operations on the lattice; $\times$ is the parallel product; $\star$ is the compositional product (the maximum of $f \circ g'$ over $f' \equiv_{\mathrm{W}} f$, $g' \equiv_{\mathrm{W}} g$); $\to$ is the implication / residual; ${}^{*}$ is finite parallelization; $\mathrm{b}$ is the Brattka–Pauly closure operator (e.g., the "bar" / total continuation); and $\diamond$ is the diamond operator (transfinite/iterated compositional closure).

Determine what can be said about the first-order theory
$$\mathrm{Th}(\mathcal{W};\, 0, 1, \top;\, \sqcap, \sqcup, \times, \star, \to, {}^{*}, \mathrm{b}, \diamond).$$
In particular:
(a) Is the quantifier-free fragment of this theory finitely axiomatizable?
(b) For which fragments of the signature (i.e., reducts to subsets of the operations and constants above) does the resulting structure admit a finite axiomatization of its (quantifier-free or full first-order) theory?
artifact.status_search_result: No published work was found that determines the first-order theory of the Weihrauch degrees in this rich signature, nor establishes finite axiomatizability of its quantifier-free fragment or of substantial fragments of the signature. The question is posed as an open problem in the literature on Weihrauch complexity, and search results show only related work on formalization of Weihrauch reducibility (e.g., via Γ₁ formulas) rather than an answer to the axiomatization question.

status_evidence.title: Reverse mathematics and Weihrauch analysis
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses formalization of Weihrauch reducibility via Γ₁ formulas, but does not address full first-order axiomatization of the Weihrauch degrees as an algebraic structure.
status_evidence.claim: Related formal work on Weihrauch reducibility exists but no axiomatization of Th(W; ...) is established.
